scope: Manual review of the sixteen remaining p1178 interfaces, including each conditional-law distinction, the prime/plus model classes and all printed HAM steps with retained source ambiguities.

rows.query: Searched Probability, MeasureTheory and Analysis for ANOVA and missing-data decompositions; inspected conditional expectation and measurable factorization definitions and proofs against the complete frozen recursion.
rows.result: Conditional expectation and factorization through the masked covariate support the recursive construction, but version choices, reconstruction and any claimed orthogonality require separate arguments.
rows.gap: Construct the components recursively along the strict pattern order, choose compatible masked-covariate versions and prove the stated reconstruction without assuming independent coordinates.

comparisons.D11: Begin with the constant E eta(X)-1/2=P(Y=1)-1/2. For each nonzero pattern, condition the entire residual eta(X)-1/2-sum over all strict predecessors f_omega'(X) on the sigma-algebra generated by X^omega. Conditional expectation is defined for integrable residuals on the valid sub-sigma-algebra, and measurable factorization yields a function of the masked covariate when its hypotheses are met. The strict order is well founded by increasing Hamming weight, and all predecessors, not just immediate ones, occur in the subtraction. The recursion uses the unconditional test-pair law P rather than a law conditioned on O. Conditional expectations supply almost-everywhere identities; the displayed reconstruction as chosen functions needs compatible versions and cannot be obtained by treating arbitrary values on null fibers as canonical. No coordinate independence is assumed, and no alternate Hoeffding decomposition or orthogonality theorem from the excluded supplementary Proposition S3 is imported.

rows.query: Searched for lower-density interfaces and inspected finite-measure real values and conditional-complete-lattice infimum bounds against the source open-ball ratio definition.
rows.result: The real infimum of nonnegative open-ball probability ratios is supported; its range and measurability as a function of the center need additional arguments.
rows.gap: Define the infimum over radii in (0,1), prove its [0,1] range and establish measurability for the subsequent tail events.

comparisons.D18: For fixed x, form the real ratios nu.real(B_r(x))/r^s for 0<r<1 and s in [0,d]. This set is nonempty and bounded below by zero, so csInf_le and le_csInf_iff give a genuine infimum without an attaining radius. Each denominator is positive. The claimed upper bound one follows by considering radii approaching one and the probability bound, not by inserting the excluded radius r=1 or claiming every ratio is at most one. Open Euclidean balls must be retained. The exponent can be less than ambient d, as for a zero-filled pattern distribution; no Lebesgue density or positive uniform lower bound is assumed. Real measure evaluation is faithful because nu is a probability. An uncountable infimum of measurable functions is not automatically measurable, so the later event use needs a specific lower-density measurability argument rather than a generic infimum shortcut.

rows.query: Inspected real event probability and compared the exact strict-margin event, all-positive-threshold quantifier and alpha domain.
rows.result: The source margin class is a direct event-probability bound under the unconditional feature measure.
rows.gap: Define the class with mu{|eta-1/2|<t} bounded by C_M*t^alpha for every positive t, including ties in the event.

comparisons.D23: Measure.real under the feature probability law expresses the left side with the event abs(eta(x)-1/2)<t. The inequality is strict at the upper threshold and includes eta=1/2; it is not the frequently used alternative 0<abs(eta-1/2)<=t. Require the bound for every t>0 with alpha>=0 and C_M>=1. At alpha=0 the right side is C_M and the condition gives no exclusion of exact ties; for alpha>0 the all-t bound forces the tie mass to vanish after a limiting argument. The probability is over unconditional test features, not conditional training features or empirical margins, and the chosen eta version must make the event measurable.

rows.query: Searched for missing-data mechanisms and inspected event conditioning, conditional expectation and factorization through a generating covariate map; compared every mask and support quantifier.
rows.result: Event-conditioned laws and regression representatives can be constructed, but the source's everywhere-on-support equality is an additional model restriction beyond ordinary almost-everywhere conditional expectation identities.
rows.gap: Choose subvector regression versions under the unconditional and positive-mask-conditioned laws and impose their equality at every specified support point.

comparisons.D10: First require Q(O=o)>0 for every o in the supplied O, making ProbabilityTheory.cond on that event a probability law. Obtain regression versions for the label indicator given X^omega under Q and under each conditioned law. The definition requires equality for every x in supp(mu), every pattern omega and every compatible o with omega preceq o. Conditional expectation and measurable factorization only construct versions and almost-everywhere guarantees; they do not enforce equality at all support points or identify values on otherwise null fibers. O need not be the entire support of the mask law, and positive probability outside O is permitted. The equation constrains the label regression for available subvectors; it does not impose independence of O from X or Y, missing completely at random, a standard missing-at-random factorization, or independent feature coordinates.

rows.query: Inspected the normalized restricted event law and measurable pushforward, and compared the conditional masked-feature probability formula and compatible-mask domain.
rows.result: Condition on a positive-probability mask event and push forward by the fixed masking map to obtain the exact conditional training-feature law.
rows.gap: Define mu_(omega|o) as the masked-feature pushforward of Q conditioned on O=o, retaining positive event mass and mask compatibility.

comparisons.D13: For o in O and omega preceq o, the missingness class gives positive Q(O=o). Apply ProbabilityTheory.cond Q {O=o}, then Measure.map by (x,y,o') maps to x^omega; measurability follows from finite coordinate masking. The resulting probability law evaluates a measurable A as Q(X^omega in A | O=o), exactly as printed. It is still a measure on R^d with zero-filled omitted coordinates. It need not equal the unconditional mu_omega because the missingness restriction equates label regression, not feature distributions. Do not reverse the roles of conditioning and dropping the mask, or use a null-event conditional fallback as if it represented an allowed source mask.

rows.query: Inspected Measure.map's measurable branch and compared the source preimage formula for the unconditional masked feature law.
rows.result: The measurable pushforward of the feature marginal under zero-filled masking gives exactly the source distribution.
rows.gap: Push the unconditional feature measure forward by x maps to x^omega as a measure on the original R^d.

comparisons.D12: Let mu be the unconditional marginal law of X and push it forward by the fixed measurable coordinate mask. Its value on A is mu({x | x^omega in A}), the source formula. The image is supported on a coordinate subspace of dimension d_omega while its ambient measurable space remains R^d; an ordinary d-dimensional density need not exist. For the zero pattern it is a Dirac law at the zero vector. Although the definition is presented for Q in the missingness class, the pushforward operation itself needs no such restriction. No conditioning on O or on complete cases is inserted, so this remains the test-feature measure used outside the original tail event.

rows.query: Inspected finite minimum nonemptiness and finite event-probability definitions; compared the source tail class with the separately printed plus condition.
rows.result: The minimum over compatible conditional lower densities and its unconditional outer probability can be assembled once the density functions and nonempty mask domains are supplied.
rows.gap: Define the strict small-density event using the compatible-mask minimum and impose its tail bound under the unconditional masked test-feature law.

comparisons.D20: For each nonzero omega, define the compatible masks C_omega={o in O | omega preceq o}. Finset.min' applied to their lower-density values at x gives the event min_o rho_(mu_(omega|o),d_omega)(x)<xi when C_omega is nonempty. Its outer probability is mu_omega, not any of the conditional measures inside the minimum. Require the bound C_L*xi^gamma_omega for every xi>0 and every nonzero omega, with Q also in Q_Miss. C_L>=1 and gamma_omega=0 are allowed by this constituent definition. Positive mass for each listed mask does not imply that C_omega is nonempty for every omega; no real-valued empty-minimum convention is supplied. Preserve the strict event and prove its measurability from the lower-density functions before treating it as the stated probability.

rows.query: Inspected event conditioning, real integral and finite minimum definitions; compared the squared-component formula and its source empty-domain limitation.
rows.result: Conditional second moments can be integrated under each positive-mask-conditioned law and minimized over a finite nonempty compatible set.
rows.gap: Construct each conditional second moment and define its compatible-mask minimum with an explicit nonempty-domain obligation.

comparisons.D14: For each compatible o, integrate f_omega(X)^2 under cond Q {O=o}. The function is the ANOVA component of the complete feature vector, even though its version depends only on the coordinates selected by omega. This is a second moment, not E[(f_omega-E[f_omega|O=o])^2|O=o]; centering would change the source. Use integrability of the square rather than the real integral's zero fallback. Finset.min' captures the minimum only after the compatible-mask set is shown nonempty, which Q_Miss by itself does not guarantee for every omega. The squared notation sigma_omega^2 names this quantity and does not separately choose a square-root parameter. The zero pattern is included in this definition, unlike the patternwise smoothness and tail exponent definitions.

rows.query: Inspected set intersection and antichain predicates and compared the component support, signal lower bounds and c_E domain in the complete class definition.
rows.result: The law class is a conjunction of the missingness model, component zero constraints and selected-pattern signal bounds; these impose no additional nonzero requirements on all predecessor components.
rows.gap: Intersect the missingness class with exact component support constraints and the stated signal lower bounds on the selected antichain.

comparisons.D17: For an antichain Omega_star and c_E in [0,1/4], retain Q in Q_Miss, require sigma_omega^2>=c_E only for omega in Omega_star, and require f_omega identically zero for all omega in U(Omega_star). U is the complement of Omega_star and its strict lower closure, including incomparable patterns. The zero restriction is printed as an identity of functions, not merely an almost-everywhere assertion or a vanishing average. Predecessor components may vanish or not; they need not all have positive signal. When c_E=0, genuine nonnegative second moments make the lower bound redundant, so this class does not then identify a uniquely nonzero maximal support. Existence of the signal minima remains a prerequisite, and HAM's later c_E>0 condition is not added to this definition.

rows.query: Inspected HolderOnWith's pseudo-emetric formulation and compared the masked Euclidean distance and all-support-point quantifiers of the source component smoothness condition.
rows.result: A Holder predicate on the pseudometric induced by masking expresses the displayed bound; using the ordinary full-coordinate metric would weaken the source restriction.
rows.gap: Equip support points with the masked Euclidean pseudometric, or factor each component through its mask, and impose HolderOnWith at beta_omega.

comparisons.D22: For each nonzero omega, the required distance is norm(x1^omega-x2^omega)_2, not norm(x1-x2)_2. HolderOnWith accommodates a pseudometric in which points with equal masked coordinates have distance zero; with exponent beta_omega>0 this forces equal f_omega values at such support points. Alternatively prove factorization and impose the Holder bound on the masked image of supp(mu). Use the common C_S>=1 and the minimum selected-coordinate exponent beta_omega in (0,1]. The quantifier is every pair of points in the feature-law support, not merely almost every pair or all points in R^d. This is a family of conditions on ANOVA components of P and is not interchangeable with one full-coordinate Holder condition on eta or a condition on the observation-mask law.

rows.query: Inspected intersection and preimage membership definitions and compared every constituent and parameter domain in the source prime minimax class.
rows.result: Intersection of the two Q-level classes and the inverse image of the P-level smoothness/margin intersection gives the exact class construction.
rows.gap: Assemble Q_E intersect Q_L intersect the P_Q-preimage of P_S intersect P_M with the printed prime-class parameter ranges.

comparisons.D24: Use Set.inter for Q_E and Q_L, and Set.preimage under Q maps to P_Q for P_S intersect P_M. The latter two properties concern the unconditional feature-label marginal rather than a mask-conditioned law. Retain Omega_star an antichain other than empty and singleton zero, c_E in [0,1/4], gamma_j>=0, beta_j in (0,1], C_L>1, C_S>=1, alpha>=0 and C_M>=1 as printed in the introduction to (11). Missingness is already required by the Q-level components. This is Q'_Miss with the original unconditional-outer-measure tail control; it does not incorporate the extra conditional outer measures of Q_L^+. Constructing the intersection proves no minimax rate and does not resolve any constituent's absent compatible-mask minimum.

rows.query: Inspected bounded real integral and conditional expectation semantics; compared the source fixed-fit test integral and its conditioning on the training data.
rows.result: Integrating the measurable zero-one loss over an independent test pair gives the conditional test error while leaving training randomness intact.
rows.gap: Define the fixed-training-data test-loss integral and prove it equals the conditional misclassification probability under the independent test experiment.

comparisons.D7: For each observed D_n, integrate the indicator C-hat(x,D_n) not equal y against the unconditional pair law P_Q. A measurable classifier makes the loss bounded and integrable under this probability measure. The result lies in [0,1] and remains a random function of the training sample. Its equality to a conditional probability given D_n uses independence and the stated test law; condExp alone does not produce that equality for a training-dependent test distribution. Later outer expectations average this training-dependent risk conditional on the entire realized mask sequence, so they must not be conflated with either the inner test integral or unconditional expected risk.

rows.query: Inspected real integration and the indicator definition, and compared the source difference-of-risks and weighted-disagreement formulas including the Bayes tie convention.
rows.result: The bounded weighted disagreement is directly integrable; its equality to excess classification risk follows from a binary conditional-risk calculation that remains to be proved.
rows.gap: Prove the binary excess-risk identity and integrate the Bayes-disagreement indicator weighted by abs(2*eta-1) under mu.

comparisons.D9: For a fixed fitted classifier, multiply the indicator that its output differs from the Bayes rule by abs(2 eta(x)-1) and integrate under the unconditional feature marginal mu. Both factors are in [0,1], so a measurable eta and classifier give a finite nonnegative integral. Comparing the two possible labels' conditional risks gives equality to L_P(C-hat)-L_P(C_Bayes); this identity is not a consequence of the indicator primitive alone. At eta=1/2 the Bayes rule chooses one but the contribution is zero even for disagreement. The result remains random through training data, and the theorem's subsequent conditional expectation over training given masks is outside this definition. No conditional training-feature measure replaces mu.

rows.query: Searched the pinned probability/analysis library for HAM, missing-data and nearest-neighbor classifiers; inspected finite sorting with its antisymmetry requirement and dependent function update; compared all 21 printed algorithm lines and the retained issue bundle.
rows.result: Finite sorting and state updates supply implementation ingredients, but no specialized HAM algorithm was found and the printed algorithm has unresolved domains, evaluation points and traversal choices.
rows.gap: Formalize the complete printed algorithm as a specification with explicit unresolved neighbor-count, tie, projection-evaluation and selection-order obligations before claiming a total implementation.

comparisons.D28: Initialize f-hat_zero by the full label average minus 1/2. In ascending Hamming dimension, process every available nonzero pattern, use the literal k=1+floor(n_omega^[2 beta_omega gamma_omega/D]) and tau=2^-4*n_omega^[-beta_omega gamma_omega/(2D)] with D=gamma_omega(2 beta_omega+d_omega)+alpha beta_omega, and collect sample indices whose masks contain omega. Reorder neighbors by the printed masked Euclidean distances, average the first k labels, subtract 1/2 and every strict-predecessor estimate, then compute the average of squared fitted components over available cases. Finset.sort can order sample indices only after a total antisymmetric tie rule is chosen; distance alone permits ties, and duplicate feature values must not erase distinct sample indices. Function.update can store successive component values, but does not fill omitted evaluations: the loop lists X_i^(o_i) whereas the signal calculation uses X_i^omega, and the reordering statement mixes original-mask pairs with omega projections and retains its subscript defect. No cap is printed; n_omega=1 gives k=2 when the exponent is defined. If gamma_omega=alpha=0 the exponent is 0/0. These are not repaired by library totalization. In descending dimension, start selected Omega empty and use literally U({omega}) intersect selected Omega empty together with signal>=tau; because U includes incomparable patterns, this differs from predecessor-only prose and can make equal-dimension traversal order consequential. Finally reconstruct 1/2 plus the sum over selected Omega union its strict lower closure and output one at equality to 1/2. If selected Omega is empty, that reconstruction omits the estimated constant component as printed. The primitives establish neither a unique total algorithm nor the risk guarantee, and no unstated capping, tie breaking, clipping or source correction is inserted.

rows.query: Inspected both finite extrema with their nonempty domains and real probability evaluation; compared Definition 3+ to the original (9) term by term.
rows.result: Nested finite extrema express the extra conditional-measure tail bound, which is strictly an additional condition alongside the original unconditional one.
rows.gap: Add the maximum conditional-outer-measure bound for the same small-density event while retaining equation (9) and all compatible-mask domain obligations.

comparisons.D29: For each nonzero omega and xi>0, define the event using the minimum over compatible o of rho_(mu_(omega|o),d_omega)(x)<xi exactly as in (9). Evaluate that same event under every compatible conditional measure mu_(omega|o-tilde), then take the maximum of those probabilities and bound it by C_L xi^gamma_omega. The inner minimizing o and outer maximizing o-tilde are independent indices over the same compatible set; they cannot be identified or collapsed into one measure. Equation (9), whose outer law is mu_omega, is also required. Finset.min' and max' enforce nonempty domains, which the general source parameters do not automatically provide. C_L=1 and gamma_omega=0 are allowed here. This class cannot be treated as equal to the original tail class simply because its events use the same conditional density functions.

rows.query: Inspected set intersection/preimage primitives and compared the source replacement instruction with equation (11), Definition 3+ and the recorded C_L domain discrepancy.
rows.result: Replacing the tail constituent in the intersection produces the HAM law class, while preserving the different source parameter ranges instead of silently reconciling them.
rows.gap: Assemble the plus class with Q_L^+ in place of Q_L and record the theorem's extension to C_L=1 separately from the introductory prime-class domain.

comparisons.D30: Construct Q_E intersect Q_L^+ intersect the P_Q-preimage of P_S intersect P_M. The plus tail class retains (9) and adds conditional outer-measure control; the support, signal, smoothness and margin constituents otherwise remain those in (11). Set intersection and preimage implement this class assembly, not a proof of HAM's guarantee or totality. The introduction to (11) prints C_L>1, while Theorem 2 allows C_L>=1 and the constituent Definitions 3/3+ allow equality. Preserve that domain extension explicitly rather than claiming the printed introductions have identical ranges. Likewise HAM's c_E>0 and sample/rate assumptions are theorem hypotheses, not automatic consequences of this set expression.
